paper_title: Analysis of atomic-clock data to constrain variations of fundamental constants
coupling_convention: dimensionless d_gamma^(1) (Damour-Donoghue linear scalar-photon coupling d_e, gravitational normalization kappa=1/(sqrt(2)M_P))
notes: Paper (NPL Sr/Yb+/Cs clock comparison, arXiv:2302.04565) constrains several couplings: d_gamma^(1), d_gamma^(2), d_me-d_g, d_q-d_g, Higgs A, and axion-gluon 1/fa. The flagship NEW exclusion is on the linear scalar-photon coupling d_gamma^(1) from the Yb+/Sr ratio, improving previous bounds by ~1 order of magnitude for 1e-20 eV < m_phi < 1e-17 eV. Data points computed from the paper's formula d^(1) = zeta_f^(1) * A_alpha(f) with zeta_f^(1) = 2.0e16 * (f/Hz) and the flat amplitude bound A_alpha(f) <= 5.6e-18 (1-sigma global WFM bound; the plotted 95% C.L. curve in Fig. 6 is only slightly higher, exact digitized values not available in text). Mass conversion m = 4.136e-15 * f[Hz] over the valid range 2.5e-6 Hz to 1.7e-2 Hz. Stochastic degradation factor ~3 already included in zeta^(1) per the paper. Assumes scalar field saturates local DM density rho_DM = 0.3 GeV/cm^3.
